learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the concepts of environment, sustainability, pollution, and treatment.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their branch of engineering.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
Understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.
Awareness of all the implications of engineering practice.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility and standards of engineering practice.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, although supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions, and to apply environmental and sustainability technologies.

syllabus_topics: Air pollution. Transport and dispersion of atmospheric pollutants
teaching_methods: Combined theoretical-practical sessions (presentations of knowledge, problem solving)
Report writing (results of practical cases and laboratory work with software)
Development of individual or group practical work (related to real environmental technology applications)
assessment_rules: In the ORDINARY CALL, an exam (50%) will be taken for each part of the course. It is necessary to obtain a MINIMUM grade of 4 in each part to pass the course. The remaining 50% is based on a case study (30%), a pollutant dispersion problem (10%), and a practical assignment (10%).
